hook.text: 'I saw the man with binoculars.' Who has the binoculars—you or the man? Your parser picks one fast.

buildup.text: Parsing is the process of assigning grammatical structure to incoming words in real time.

discovery.text: The 'minimal attachment' strategy says the parser prefers the simplest possible structure first.

twist.text: When context contradicts the initial parse, the brain backtracks—costing time and effort.

climax.text: Parsing models debate whether structure or meaning comes first—or if both operate in parallel.

punchline.text: Your brain builds a sentence tree as you hear it—one word at a time.

quiz.question: What does the minimal attachment strategy prefer?
